skill.name: nx-workspace-patterns
skill.description: Configure and optimize Nx monorepo workspaces with patterns for project boundaries, caching, CI, generators, and affected commands.
skill.summary: Guide Nx workspace structure, module boundaries, caching, CI, and generator patterns for monorepos.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives because they are Markdown fences, inline examples, TypeScript template literals, documentation links, or normal Nx configuration references. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found. One semantic issue remains: the remote cache guidance shows token fields directly in configuration, which could lead users to commit real secrets.

remediation.issue: Remote cache examples show accessToken and nxCloudAccessToken inside an nx.json style snippet.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or CI secret references in the example, and state that real cache tokens must never be committed.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Cache Token Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The remote cache example places accessToken and nxCloudAccessToken placeholders directly in an nx.json style snippet. Users may copy this pattern with real Nx Cloud tokens and commit secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show token fields inside a committed configuration example. The values are placeholders, so the risk is guidance-driven rather than active credential exposure.

content.value_statement: Nx monorepos can become slow and hard to govern as projects grow. This skill provides patterns for configuration, boundaries, caching, CI, generators, and affected commands.
actual_capabilities: Provides example nx.json settings for caching, target defaults, named inputs, and React generators.
Shows project.json patterns for web applications with build, serve, test, and lint targets.
Defines module boundary rules using Nx tags for app, feature, UI, data-access, util, and scopes.
Includes a custom generator template for feature libraries using @nx/devkit and @nx/react.
Gives CI examples for affected lint, test, build, and e2e commands.
Documents remote cache configuration examples for Nx Cloud and S3-backed cache.
limitations: It is a pattern guide, not an automated workspace migration tool.
Examples assume Nx React and Jest patterns; other stacks need adaptation.
Remote cache examples use placeholder tokens and require secure secret management.
It does not validate the current repository graph or run Nx commands itself.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Nx Workspace
use_cases.description: Design app and library layout, tags, target defaults, and initial generator defaults before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve Monorepo CI Speed
use_cases.description: Apply affected commands, cacheable targets, named inputs, and parallel settings to reduce redundant work.

use_cases.title: Enforce Project Boundaries
use_cases.description: Use tag-based dependency constraints to keep application, feature, UI, data access, and utility layers organized.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workspace Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new monorepo.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nx-workspace-patterns to plan an Nx workspace for two applications and shared libraries. Include tags, library types, and basic caching choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review Nx Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing workspace settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nx-workspace-patterns to review my nx.json approach. Check target defaults, named inputs, cacheable tasks, and generator defaults for missing patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Affected CI
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CI optimization for pull requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nx-workspace-patterns to design a pull request CI flow with affected lint, test, build, and e2e steps. Include caching and parallelism guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Define Generator Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nx-workspace-patterns to design a feature library generator strategy. Include naming, tags, file generation, formatting, and boundary alignment.

output_examples.input: I need an Nx workspace for web and API apps with shared UI and utilities.
output: Recommended apps and library groups by responsibility.
Suggested tags for app, feature, UI, data access, utility, and scope boundaries.
Initial caching and target-default choices for build, lint, test, and e2e tasks.

output_examples.input: Our CI runs every task on every pull request.
output: Affected command plan for lint, test, build, and e2e stages.
Cacheable target recommendations and named input checks.
Parallelism guidance with a safer single-threaded e2e step.

output_examples.input: We need consistent feature libraries across teams.
output: Generator responsibilities for naming, directory placement, tags, and files.
Boundary rules that keep feature, UI, data access, and utility layers separate.
Review notes for adapting the pattern to non-React stacks.

best_practices: Keep project tags consistent so module boundary rules remain enforceable.
Enable cacheable targets and named inputs early to improve local and CI feedback loops.
Store remote cache credentials in secret managers, environment variables, or CI secrets.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding cache access tokens in committed workspace configuration.
Creating many tiny libraries without clear ownership or dependency boundaries.
Bypassing affected commands and running every workspace task for every change.

faq.question: Does this skill create an Nx workspace automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and templates that you adapt to your repository.

faq.question: Can it help with existing monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to review tags, target defaults, caching, CI, and library boundaries.

faq.question: Does it require Nx Cloud?
faq.answer: No. It includes Nx Cloud and self-hosted cache examples, but remote caching is optional.

faq.question: Which frameworks do the examples target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on React, Webpack, Jest, ESLint, and standard Nx workspace patterns.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I secure before using remote cache examples?
faq.answer: Keep cache tokens out of committed files and pass them through approved secret management systems.
